doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Teddy Charles as a person and his Monk influence
summary: Charles sought something more advanced than vibes mainstream, inspired chiefly by Monk, and later ran a yacht.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Maybe there hasn’t been enough written about Teddy Charles, is there something that you can add about Teddy Charles; what it was like to work with him or as a person?

No, the only thing that I can say basically was that he was trying to find another area. He was content just playing the vibes like Milt Jackson or Lionel Hampton. He wanted to do something that was more advanced. There was no audience for it … He’s not in music now. He’s has a yacht. He rents the yacht and takes people on cruises, and he’s happy doing that, which I can understand.
Did you know or do you remember what inspired him or influenced him as far as his musical direction? Was he listening to particular things? Was he studying scores?
I think Monk inspired him. I think that was the basic inspiration, Monk. Other than Monk, it was Charlie Parker, with more Monk than anything else.
